method: Manual review against the unchanged frozen five factual and five attribution obligations. Scores count met requirements, not true-sentence percentages. Actor judgments assess the implementing component separately from mechanics and literal citation accuracy; a file label can identify its component while failing canonical citation precision.

results.review: Correct user-role memory, lookup/run, and tool-role memory for subsequent LLM processing in the Agent.run loop. Visible generate arguments are reproduced but active-provider acquisition is omitted. No name/args extraction or main startup. The closing statement attributes the whole processing loop to Agent.run, including execution and feedback.
results.citation_review: CLI and Agent.run identified; main omitted. Invents tool_call_entry in a purported source snippet and calls exit/quit key-command examples. Datetime-service guesses exceed the frozen source.

results.review: Correct normal input/user-memory and role-tool memory/next-iteration feedback. Agent is explicitly named as the execution and memory owner. Provider acquisition/arguments, name/args extraction, lookup/run and main are absent or replaced with nonexistent calls.
results.citation_review: Invents self.llm.generate(messages), tool.execute(tool_call), prompt = input(">>> ") and assistant record shape. Uses #Agent instead of supplied #Agent.run. Its claim that all references match source is false.

results.review: All five complete factual obligations have omissions: user-role append, provider arguments/acquisition, name/args extraction, lookup, and role-tool memory are not explained. Agent.run is correctly identified as executor and owner of result append/next LLM call. Calling the CLI loop startup does not account for main.
results.citation_review: Correct Agent.run tool_call response getter and tool.run expression. Several quote cells are ellipsis paraphrases rather than literal source; main omitted. input() omits the actual prompt and strip operation.

results.review: Correct user-role append and role-tool memory reused on the next iteration. Agent owns input memory, execution, and feedback. Omits provider arguments/acquisition, actual field extraction, lookup/argument dispatch and main.
results.citation_review: CLI/Agent.run identified; main omitted. Illustrative tool_call uses arguments instead of actual args. Examples are disclosed as illustrative, not literal excerpts.

results.review: Correct normal-path user-role memory and Agent-owned tool-role feedback into the second LLM call. Omits provider parameters/acquisition, extraction, lookup/run and main. The later always-next-iteration statement is an unsupported generalization beyond the declared normal-path scope; max_steps and pruning qualify the broader claim.
results.citation_review: CLI/Agent.run location table is correct for normal input and memory operations; main omitted. Datetime outputs are examples. No literal support for final-answer branches is in the frozen excerpt set.

results.review: CLI and agent-file rows correctly own input, user-memory, execution and role-tool feedback to the next generation. Provider argument expression is present but active acquisition is absent. No name/args extraction, tool lookup or main. Calls the trace typical AI pseudocode and adds an unrelated framework analogy.
results.citation_review: Basename file labels identify components but lack requested canonical methods. Invents build_messages/process_response/execute_tool/append_result handoffs. Replaces canonical assistant record with [tool_call], calls tool a function and self.tools a list; multiple snippet cells are rewritten pseudocode despite the literal-quote instruction.

limits: Three stochastic paired runs on one development question. No statistical superiority claim. State-dependency omission remains in both arms; no capability ceiling is established. Literal/source citation defects are reviewed separately from actor attribution.
